metadata.technology_specification: Triple Quadrupole Liquid Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry (Triple Quadrupole LC–MS) System
metadata.technology_reasoning: Triple Quadrupole LC–MS systems are the industry standard for targeted quantitative analysis in bioanalytics and environmental testing due to their high specificity, sensitivity, and selectivity, comprising multiple quadrupole mass filters operated in series coupled with liquid chromatography for sample separation.

components.reasoning: The LC module is essential for separating complex mixtures before mass analysis and is a separate, industry-standard subassembly procured or built independently.
The ion source generates ions from the sample for mass analysis; it is a distinct, often replaceable unit crucial for system operation.
Q1 acts as the first mass filter selecting precursor ions; it is a core component always present and separately manufactured within the mass analyzer.
The collision cell induces fragmentation via collision-induced dissociation; critical for triple quadrupole operation and a separate major subassembly.
Q3 filters product ions generated in Q2; an indispensable and separately produced module for MS/MS analysis.
The detector records ion signals; it is a specialized, separate component fundamental for data acquisition.
Maintains high vacuum conditions needed for ion transmission and detection; consists of pumps and vacuum chambers which are separate components.
Includes the system's electronic control boards, signal processing, and data acquisition hardware; always present and sourced separately as a complex subassembly.
Automates sample introduction into LC; standard in modern systems though optional in some basic configurations.
Structural housing for all components; typically a separately manufactured assembly providing mechanical support and environmental protection.
